Aparampi imasmiṃ ṭhāne hetukittanaṃ nāma gahitaṃ. Tihetukakammañhi tihetukampi duhetukampi ahetukampi vipākaṃ deti. Duhetukakammaṃ tihetukavipākaṃ na deti, itaraṃ deti. Tihetukakammena paṭisandhi tihetukāpi hoti, duhetukāpi; ahetukā na hoti. Duhetukena duhetukāpi hoti ahetukāpi; tihetukā na hoti. Asaṅkhārikaṃ kusalaṃ asaṅkhārikampi sasaṅkhārikampi [V 0.0307] vipākaṃ deti. Sasaṅkhārikaṃ [P 0.0269] sasaṅkhārikampi asaṅkhārikampi vipākaṃ deti. Ārammaṇena vedanā parivattetabbā. Javanena tadārammaṇaṃ niyāmetabbaṃ.

Furthermore, in this context, a discourse called the 'Enumeration of Roots' is taken up. Triple-rooted kamma gives a triple-rooted, double-rooted, and rootless result. Double-rooted kamma does not give a triple-rooted result, but gives the other. By triple-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking can be triple-rooted or double-rooted; it is not rootless. By double-rooted kamma, it can be double-rooted or rootless; it is not triple-rooted. Unprompted wholesome kamma gives both an unprompted and a prompted result. Prompted wholesome kamma gives both a prompted and an unprompted result. Feeling should be changed by the object. Registration should be determined by impulsion.

Idāni tassa tassa therassa vāde soḷasamaggādayo veditabbā. Paṭhamakāmāvacarakusalasadisena hi paṭhamamahāvipākacittena gahitapaṭisandhikassa gabbhāvāsato nikkhamitvā saṃvarāsaṃvare paṭṭhapetuṃ samatthabhāvaṃ upagatassa cakkhudvārasmiṃ ‘iṭṭhārammaṇe’ āpāthamāgate kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅge anāvaṭṭiteyeva atikkamanaārammaṇānaṃ pamāṇaṃ natthi. Kasmā evaṃ hoti? Ārammaṇadubbalatāya. Ayaṃ tāva eko moghavāro.

Now, in the view of each of those elders, the group of sixteen results and so on should be understood. For one who has taken rebirth-linking with the first great resultant consciousness, which is similar to the first sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, who, having emerged from the womb, has become capable of establishing restraint and non-restraint: when a desirable object has come into range at the eye-door, before the life-continuum has even been adverted to by the functional mind-element, there is no measure of the objects that have passed by. Why is it so? Due to the weakness of the object. This, for a start, is one futile occasion.

Sace pana bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti, kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅge āvaṭṭite, voṭṭhabbanaṃ apāpetvāva antarā, cakkhuviññāṇe vā sampaṭicchane vā santīraṇe [M 0.0310] vā ṭhatvā nivattissatīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Voṭṭhabbanavasena pana ṭhatvā ekaṃ vā dve vā cittāni pavattanti. Tato āsevanaṃ labhitvā javanaṭṭhāne ṭhatvā puna bhavaṅgaṃ otarati idampi ārammaṇadubbalatāya eva hoti. Ayaṃ pana vāro ‘diṭṭhaṃ viya me, sutaṃ viya me’tiādīni vadanakāle labbhati. Ayampi dutiyo moghavāro.

On the other hand, if it turns the life-continuum, when the life-continuum has been turned by the functional mind-element, the case where, without reaching the determining consciousness, it would stop at eye-consciousness, receiving, or investigating in between and then recede, does not exist. Rather, having stopped by way of the determining consciousness, one or two consciousnesses arise. Thereafter, having obtained repetition and being established at the stage of impulsion, it again sinks into the life-continuum. This too occurs due to the weakness of the object. This occasion, however, is obtained at the time of saying, 'It is as if seen by me,' 'It is as if heard by me,' and so on. This too is the second futile occasion.

Aparassa kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅge āvaṭṭite vīthicittāni uppajjanti, javanaṃ javati. Javanapariyosāne pana tadārammaṇassa vāro. Tasmiṃ anuppanneyeva bhavaṅgaṃ otarati. Tatrāyaṃ upamā – yathā hi nadiyā āvaraṇaṃ bandhitvā mahāmātikābhimukhe udake kate udakaṃ gantvā ubhosu tīresu kedāre pūretvā atirekaṃ kakkaṭakamaggādīhi palāyitvā puna nadiṃyeva otarati, evametaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ettha hi nadiyaṃ udakappavattanakālo viya bhavaṅgavīthippavattanakālo[P 0.0270]. Āvaraṇabandhanakālo viya kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭanakālo. Mahāmātikāya udakappavattanakālo viya vīthicittappavatti. Ubhosu tīresu kedārapūraṇaṃ viya javanaṃ. Kakkaṭakamaggādīhi palāyitvā puna udakassa nadīotaraṇaṃ viya javanaṃ javitvā tadārammaṇe anuppanneyeva puna bhavaṅgotaraṇaṃ. Evaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ otaraṇacittānampi gaṇanapatho natthi. Idañcāpi ārammaṇadubbalatāya eva hoti. Ayaṃ tatiyo moghavāro.

In another case, when the life-continuum has been turned by the functional mind-element, process consciousnesses arise, and the impulsion impels. At the end of the impulsion, however, it is the turn of the registering consciousness. Even before that has arisen, it sinks into the life-continuum. Herein, this is the simile: Just as when a dam is built in a river and the water is made to face a great canal, the water flows, fills the fields on both banks, and the excess, escaping through crab-paths and the like, flows back into the river itself—so should this be understood. Herein, the time of the water's flow in the river is like the time of the life-continuum process's flow. The time of building the dam is like the time of the turning of the life-continuum by the functional mind-element. The time of the water's flow in the great canal is like the occurrence of process consciousness. The filling of the fields on both banks is like the impulsion. The escaping through crab-paths and the like and the water's subsequent return to the river is like, after the impulsion has impelled, the subsequent sinking back into the life-continuum even before the registering consciousness has arisen. Thus, there is no way of counting the consciousnesses that sink into the life-continuum. This too occurs due to the weakness of the object. This is the third futile occasion.

Sace pana balavārammaṇaṃ āpāthagataṃ hoti kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅge āvaṭṭite cakkhuviññāṇādīni [V 0.0308] uppajjanti. Javanaṭṭhāne pana paṭhamakāmāvacarakusalacittaṃ javanaṃ hutvā chasattavāre javitvā tadārammaṇassa vāraṃ deti. Tadārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhahamānaṃ taṃsadisameva mahāvipākacittaṃ patiṭṭhāti. Idaṃ dve nāmāni labhati – paṭisandhicittasadisattā ‘mūlabhavaṅga’nti ca, yaṃ javanena gahitaṃ ārammaṇaṃ tassa gahitattā ‘tadārammaṇa’nti ca. Imasmiṃ ṭhāne cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ santīraṇaṃ tadārammaṇanti cattāri vipākacittāni gaṇanūpagāni honti.

But if a strong object comes into range, when the life-continuum has been turned by the functional mind-element, eye-consciousness and so forth arise. At the stage of impulsion, however, the first sense-sphere wholesome consciousness, having become an impulsion and having impelled for six or seven times, gives the turn to the registering consciousness. When the registering consciousness is being established, a great resultant consciousness that is just like it is established. This obtains two names: 'root life-continuum' because of its similarity to the rebirth-linking consciousness, and 'registering consciousness' because of its grasping that object which was grasped by the impulsion. In this case, four resultant consciousnesses—eye-consciousness, receiving, investigating, and registering—come to be counted.

Yadā pana dutiyakusalacittaṃ javanaṃ hoti, tadā taṃsadisaṃ dutiyavipākacittameva tadārammaṇaṃ hutvā patiṭṭhāti. Idañca dve nāmāni labhati[M 0.0311]. Paṭisandhicittena asadisattā ‘āgantukabhavaṅga’nti ca purimanayeneva ‘tadārammaṇa’nti ca. Iminā saddhiṃ purimāni cattāri pañca honti.

But when the second wholesome consciousness is the impulsion, then the second resultant consciousness, being similar to it, is established, having become the registering consciousness. And this obtains two names: 'adventitious life-continuum' because of its dissimilarity to the rebirth-linking consciousness, and 'registering consciousness' in the same way as before. Together with this, the previous four become five.

Yadā pana tatiyakusalacittaṃ javanaṃ hoti, tadā taṃsadisaṃ tatiyavipākacittaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hutvā patiṭṭhāti. Idampi vuttanayeneva ‘āgantukabhavaṅgaṃ’‘tadārammaṇa’nti ca dve nāmāni labhati. Iminā saddhiṃ purimāni pañca cha honti.

But when the third wholesome consciousness is the impulsion, then the third resultant consciousness, being similar to it, is established, having become the registering consciousness. This too, in the aforesaid manner, obtains the two names 'adventitious life-continuum' and 'registering consciousness.' Together with this, the previous five become six.

Yadā pana catutthakusalacittaṃ javanaṃ hoti, tadā taṃsadisaṃ catutthavipākacittaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hutvā patiṭṭhāti. Idampi vuttanayeneva ‘āgantukabhavaṅgaṃ’‘tadārammaṇa’nti [P 0.0271] ca dve nāmāni labhati. Iminā saddhiṃ purimāni cha satta honti.

But when the fourth wholesome consciousness is the impulsion, then the fourth resultant consciousness, being similar to it, is established, having become the registering consciousness. This too, in the aforesaid manner, obtains the two names 'adventitious life-continuum' and 'registering consciousness.' Together with this, the previous six become seven.

Yadā pana tasmiṃ dvāre ‘iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇaṃ’ āpāthamāgacchati, tatrāpi vuttanayeneva tayo moghavārā labbhanti. Yasmā pana ārammaṇena vedanā parivattati tasmā tattha upekkhāsahagatasantīraṇaṃ. Catunnañca upekkhāsahagatamahākusalajavanānaṃ pariyosāne cattāri upekkhāsahagatamahāvipākacittāneva tadārammaṇabhāvena patiṭṭhahanti. Tānipi vuttanayeneva ‘āgantukabhavaṅgaṃ’‘tadārammaṇa’nti ca dve nāmāni labhanti. ‘Piṭṭhibhavaṅgānī’tipi vuccanti eva. Iti imāni pañca purimehi sattahi saddhiṃ dvādasa honti. Evaṃ cakkhudvāre dvādasa, sotadvārādīsu dvādasa dvādasāti, samasaṭṭhi honti. Evaṃ ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite samasaṭṭhi [V 0.0309] vipākacittāni uppajjanti. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana cakkhudvāre dvādasa, sotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇāni cattārīti soḷasa honti.

But when at that door a moderately desirable object comes into range, there too, in the aforesaid manner, the three futile occasions are obtained. And since feeling changes according to the object, therefore the investigating consciousness there is one accompanied by equanimity. At the end of the four great wholesome impulsions accompanied by equanimity, four great resultant consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity are themselves established as the registering consciousness. Those too, in the aforesaid manner, obtain the two names 'adventitious life-continuum' and 'registering consciousness.' They are also called 'backing life-continuums.' Thus, these five, together with the previous seven, become twelve. In this way, there are twelve in the eye-door, and twelve each in the ear-door and so forth, making exactly sixty. Thus, when kamma is generated by a single volition, exactly sixty resultant consciousnesses arise. But by way of taking what has not been taken, in the eye-door there are twelve, and the four—ear, nose, tongue, and body consciousnesses—making sixteen.

Imasmiṃ ṭhāne ambopamaṃ nāma gaṇhiṃsu – eko kira puriso phalitambarukkhamūle sasīsaṃ pārupitvā nipanno niddāyati. Athekaṃ ambapakkaṃ vaṇṭato muccitvā tassa kaṇṇasakkhaliṃ puñchamānaṃ viya ‘tha’nti bhūmiyaṃ pati. So tassa saddena pabujjhitvā ummīletvā olokesi. Tato hatthaṃ pasāretvā phalaṃ gahetvā madditvā upasiṅghitvā paribhuñji.

In this context, they took up what is called the Mango Simile. It is said that a certain man, having covered his body including his head, was lying down asleep at the foot of a mango tree laden with fruit. Then a ripe mango, released from its stalk, fell to the ground with a 'thud,' as if touching his ear. Awakened by its sound, he opened his eyes and looked. Then, stretching out his hand, he took the fruit, squeezed it, smelled it, and consumed it.

Tattha, tassa purisassa ambarukkhamūle niddāyanakālo viya bhavaṅgasamaṅgikālo. Ambapakkassa vaṇṭato muccitvā kaṇṇasakkhaliṃ puñchamānassa patanakālo viya ārammaṇassa pasādaghaṭṭanakālo. Tena saddena pabuddhakālo [M 0.0312] viya kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭitakālo. Ummīletvā olokitakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇassa dassanakiccasādhanakālo. Hatthaṃ pasāretvā gahitakālo viya vipākamanodhātuyā ārammaṇassa sampaṭicchitakālo. Gahetvā madditakālo viya vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa santīraṇakālo. Upasiṅghitakālo viya kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa vavatthāpitakālo[P 0.0272]. Paribhuttakālo viya javanassa ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhavitakālo. Ayaṃ upamā kiṃ dīpeti? Ārammaṇassa pasādaghaṭṭanameva kiccaṃ. Tena pasāde ghaṭṭite kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgāvaṭṭanameva, cakkhuviññāṇassa dassanamattakameva, vipākamanodhātuyā ārammaṇasampaṭicchanamattakameva, vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇasantīraṇamattakameva, kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇavavatthāpanamattakameva kiccaṃ. Ekantena pana ārammaṇarasaṃ javanameva anubhavatīti dīpeti.

Therein, for that man, the time of sleeping at the foot of the mango tree is like the time when the life-continuum is present. The moment the ripe mango detaches from its stalk and falls while brushing against the ear is like the moment when the object strikes the sensitive faculty. The time of being awakened by that sound is like the time when the life-continuum is averted by the functional mind-element. The time of opening the eyes and looking is like the time when eye-consciousness accomplishes its task of seeing. The time of reaching out the hand and grasping is like the time when the resultant mind-element receives the object. The time of grasping and squeezing is like the time when the resultant mind-consciousness-element investigates the object. The time of smelling it is like the time when the functional mind-consciousness-element determines the object. The time of consuming it is like the time when the impulsion experiences the flavour of the object. What does this simile illustrate? The striking of the object on the sensitive faculty is merely the function. When the sensitive faculty is struck, the aversion of the life-continuum by the functional mind-element is merely the function; the mere seeing by eye-consciousness is merely the function; the mere receiving of the object by the resultant mind-element is merely the function; the mere investigating of the object by the resultant mind-consciousness-element is merely the function; the mere determining of the object by the functional mind-consciousness-element is merely the function. But it illustrates that the impulsion alone certainly experiences the flavour of the object.

Ettha ca ‘tvaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ nāma hohi, tvaṃ āvajjanaṃ nāma, tvaṃ dassanaṃ nāma, tvaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ nāma, tvaṃ santīraṇaṃ nāma, tvaṃ voṭṭhabbanaṃ nāma, tvaṃ javanaṃ nāma, hohī’ti koci kattā vā kāretā vā natthi.

And herein, there is no agent or instigator who says, 'You, be what is called the life-continuum! You, be what is called adverting! You, be what is called seeing! You, be what is called receiving! You, be what is called investigating! You, be what is called determining! You, be what is called impulsion!'

Imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne pañcavidhaṃ niyāmaṃ nāma gaṇhiṃsu – bījaniyāmaṃ utuniyāmaṃ kammaniyāmaṃ dhammaniyāmaṃ cittaniyāmanti. Tattha kulatthagacchassa uttaraggabhāvo, dakkhiṇavalliyā dakkhiṇato [V 0.0310] rukkhapariharaṇaṃ, sūriyāvaṭṭapupphānaṃ sūriyābhimukhabhāvo, māluvalatāya rukkhābhimukhagamanameva, nāḷikerassa matthake chiddasabbhāvoti tesaṃ tesaṃ bījānaṃ taṃtaṃsadisaphaladānaṃ bījaniyāmo nāma. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ samaye tesaṃ tesaṃ rukkhānaṃ ekappahāreneva pupphaphalapallavaggahaṇaṃ utuniyāmo nāma. Tihetukakammaṃ tihetukaduhetukāhetukavipākaṃ deti. Duhetukakammaṃ duhetukāhetukavipākaṃ deti, tihetukaṃ na detīti, evaṃ tassa tassa kammassa taṃtaṃsadisavipākadānameva kammaniyāmo nāma.

Furthermore, in this context, they took up five kinds of fixed orders: the seed-order, the seasonal-order, the kamma-order, the Dhamma-order, and the mind-order. Herein, the horse gram bush having its tip to the north, the right-turning creeper circling a tree from the right, the sunflower facing the sun, the māluvā creeper going only towards a tree, and the existence of a hole at the top of a coconut—the giving of a corresponding fruit by each respective seed is called the seed-order. At each respective time, the simultaneous bearing of flowers, fruits, and shoots by those respective trees is called the seasonal-order. Three-rooted kamma gives three-rooted, two-rooted, or rootless resultants. Two-rooted kamma gives two-rooted or rootless resultants, but not a three-rooted resultant. Thus, the giving of a corresponding resultant by each respective kamma is called the kamma-order.

Aparopi kammasarikkhakavipākavaseneva kammaniyāmo hoti. Tassa dīpanatthamidaṃ vatthuṃ kathenti – sammāsambuddhakāle sāvatthiyā dvāragāmo jhāyi[M 0.0313]. Tato pajjalitaṃ tiṇakaraḷaṃ uṭṭhahitvā ākāsena gacchato kākassa gīvāya paṭimuñci. So viravanto bhūmiyaṃ patitvā kālamakāsi. Mahāsamuddepi [P 0.0273] ekā nāvā niccalā aṭṭhāsi. Heṭṭhā kenaci niruddhabhāvaṃ apassantā kāḷakaṇṇisalākaṃ vicāresuṃ. Sā nāvikasseva upāsikāya hatthe pati. Tato ekissā kāraṇā mā sabbe nassantu, udake naṃ khipāmāti āhaṃsu. Nāviko ‘na sakkhissāmi etaṃ udake uppilavamānaṃ passitu’nti vālikāghaṭaṃ gīvāyaṃ bandhāpetvā khipāpesi. Taṅkhaṇaññeva nāvā khittasaro viya pakkhandi. Eko bhikkhu leṇe vasati. Mahantaṃ pabbatakūṭaṃ patitvā dvāraṃ pidahi. Taṃ sattame divase sayameva apagataṃ. Sammāsambuddhassa jetavane nisīditvā dhammaṃ kathentassa imāni tīṇi vatthūni ekappahāreneva ārocesuṃ. Satthā ‘na etaṃ aññehi kataṃ, tehi katakammameva ta’nti atītaṃ āharitvā dassento āha –

Furthermore, the kamma-order also operates precisely through the power of the result being similar to the kamma. To illustrate this, they tell the following story: During the time of the Perfectly Enlightened One, a village near the gate of Sāvatthī was burning. Then a blazing bundle of grass rose up and, flying through the sky, became fastened to the neck of a crow. Crying out, it fell to the ground and died. Also, in the great ocean, a ship stood motionless. Seeing no obstruction below, they cast lots to find the ill-omened one. The lot fell into the hand of the ship-captain's laywoman follower. Then they said, 'On account of one woman, let not all of us perish! Let us throw her into the water.' The captain, thinking, 'I cannot bear to see her floating on the water,' had a pot of sand tied to her neck and had her thrown in. At that very moment, the ship shot forward like a released arrow. A monk was dwelling in a cave. A large mountain peak fell and closed the entrance. On the seventh day, it moved away by itself. While the Perfectly Enlightened One was seated in Jetavana, teaching the Dhamma, these three incidents were reported to him at once. The Teacher, bringing forth the past in order to show that 'This was not done by others, but is the very deed done by them,' said—

Kāko purimattabhāve manusso hutvā ekaṃ duṭṭhagoṇaṃ dametuṃ asakkonto gīvāya palālaveṇiṃ bandhitvā aggiṃ adāsi. Goṇo teneva mato. Idāni taṃ kammaṃ etassa ākāsena gacchatopi na muccituṃ adāsi. Sāpi itthī purimattabhāve ekā itthīyeva. Eko kukkuro tāya paricito hutvā araññaṃ gacchantiyā saddhiṃ gacchati, saddhimevāgacchati. Manussā ‘nikkhanto idāni amhākaṃ sunakhaluddako’ti uppaṇḍenti. Sā tena aṭṭīyamānā kukkuraṃ nivāretuṃ asakkontī vālikāghaṭaṃ gīvāya bandhitvā udake khipi. Taṃ kammaṃ tassā samuddamajjhe muccituṃ nādāsi. Sopi bhikkhu purimattabhāve gopālako hutvā bilaṃ paviṭṭhāya godhāya sākhābhaṅgamuṭṭhiyā dvāraṃ thakesi. Tato sattame divase sayaṃ āgantvā vivari. Godhā kampamānā [V 0.0311] nikkhami. Karuṇāya taṃ na māresi. Taṃ kammaṃ tassa pabbatantaraṃ pavisitvā nisinnassa muccituṃ nādāsīti. Imāni tīṇi vatthūni samodhānetvā imaṃ gāthamāha –

The crow, in a former existence, was a man who, being unable to tame a vicious ox, tied a bundle of straw to its neck and set it on fire. The ox died because of that. Now, that kamma did not allow him to escape, even while flying through the sky. That woman too, in a former existence, was a woman. A dog, having become familiar with her, would go with her to the forest and would return together with her. People would mock her, saying, 'Now our dog-hunter has gone out!' Distressed by this and unable to stop the dog, she tied a pot of sand to its neck and threw it into the water. That kamma did not allow her to be freed, even in the middle of the ocean. That monk too, in a former existence, was a cowherd who blocked the entrance of a hole which a lizard had entered with a handful of broken branches. On the seventh day, he himself returned and opened it. The lizard came out trembling. Out of compassion, he did not kill it. That kamma did not allow him to be freed when he had entered into a mountain and was seated there. Having connected these three stories, he spoke this verse:

“Na antalikkhe na samuddamajjhe,

Na [P 0.0274] pabbatānaṃ vivaraṃ pavissa;

Na vijjate so jagatippadeso,

Yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā”ti. (dha. pa. 127);

Neither in the sky, nor in the midst of the ocean, nor by entering a mountain cave, is there found any place on earth where one may escape from an evil deed.

Ayampi [M 0.0314] kammaniyāmoyeva nāma. Aññānipi evarūpāni vatthūni kathetabbāni.

This too is indeed the kamma-order. Other such stories should also be told.

Bodhisattānaṃ pana paṭisandhiggahaṇe, mātukucchito nikkhamane, abhisambodhiyaṃ tathāgatassa dhammacakkappavattane, āyusaṅkhārassa ossajjane, parinibbāne ca dasasahassacakkavāḷakampanaṃ dhammaniyāmo nāma.

Furthermore, at the time of a Bodhisatta's taking of rebirth-linking, at the time of his emerging from his mother's womb, at his supreme enlightenment, at the Tathāgata's setting in motion the Wheel of Dhamma, at the relinquishing of the life-formation, and at the Parinibbāna, the trembling of the ten-thousand-world-system is called the Order of the Norm.

Ārammaṇena pana pasāde ghaṭṭite ‘tvaṃ āvajjanaṃ nāma hohi…pe… tvaṃ javanaṃ nāma hohī’ti koci kattā vā kāretā vā natthi, attano attano pana dhammatāya eva ārammaṇena pasādassa ghaṭṭitakālato paṭṭhāya kiriyamanodhātucittaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ dassanakiccaṃ sādheti, vipākamanodhātu sampaṭicchanakiccaṃ sādheti, vipākamanoviññāṇadhātu santīraṇakiccaṃ sādheti, kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātu voṭṭhabbanakiccaṃ sādheti, javanaṃ ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhavatīti ayaṃ cittaniyāmo nāma. Ayaṃ idha adhippeto.

Furthermore, when an object strikes a sensitive faculty, there is no agent or instigator who says, ‘You, become what is called adverting… you, become what is called impulsion.’ Rather, by its own nature, from the moment the object strikes the sensitive faculty, the functional mind-element consciousness turns the life-continuum, eye-consciousness accomplishes the function of seeing, ... and impulsion experiences the taste of the object. This is called the Order of Consciousness. This is what is intended here.

Sasaṅkhārikatihetukakusalenāpi upekkhāsahagatehi asaṅkhārikasasaṅkhārikakusalacittehipi kamme āyūhite taṃsadisavipākacittehi ādinnāya paṭisandhiyā eseva nayo. Upekkhāsahagatadvaye pana paṭhamaṃ ‘iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇavasena’ pavattiṃ dassetvā pacchā ‘iṭṭhārammaṇavasena’ dassetabbā.

Even when kamma is generated by prompted, three-rooted wholesome consciousness, or by unprompted and prompted wholesome consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, this is the same method for the rebirth-linking taken by similar resultant consciousnesses. However, regarding the two accompanied by equanimity, first, the process should be shown ‘by way of a neutral desirable object,’ and afterwards, ‘by way of a desirable object.’

Evampi ekekasmiṃ dvāre dvādasa dvādasa hutvā samasaṭṭhi honti. Aggahitaggahaṇena soḷasa vipākacittāni uppajjanti.

Thus, at each door, there being twelve each, they become sixty in total. By taking what has not yet been taken, sixteen resultant consciousnesses arise.

Imasmiṃ [V 0.0312] ṭhāne pañcaucchunāḷiyantopamaṃ nāma gaṇhiṃsu. Ucchupīḷanasamaye kira ekasmā gāmā ekādasa yantavāhā nikkhamitvā ekaṃ ucchuvāṭaṃ disvā tassa paripakkabhāvaṃ ñatvā ucchusāmikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ‘yantavāhā [P 0.0275] maya’nti ārocesuṃ. So ‘ahaṃ tumheyeva pariyesāmī’ti ucchusālaṃ te gahetvā agamāsi. Te tattha nāḷiyantaṃ sajjetvā ‘mayaṃ ekādasa janā, aparampi ekaṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭati, vetanena gaṇhathā’ti āhaṃsu. Ucchusāmiko ‘ahameva sahāyo bhavissāmī’ti ucchūnaṃ sālaṃ pūrāpetvā tesaṃ sahāyo ahosi. Te attano attano kiccāni katvā, phāṇitapācakena [M 0.0315] ucchurase pakke, guḷabandhakena baddhe, ucchusāmikena tulayitvā bhāgesu dinnesu, attano attano bhāgaṃ ādāya ucchusālaṃ sāmikassa paṭicchāpetvā, eteneva upāyena aparāsupi catūsu sālāsu kammaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.

In this context, the ancient teachers adopted the simile of the five sugarcane presses. It is said that at the time of pressing sugarcane, eleven press operators went out from a village and, seeing a sugarcane field and knowing its ripeness, they approached the owner of the sugarcane and announced, ‘We are press operators.’ He said, ‘I was looking for you,’ and taking them, he went to the sugarcane shed. There, they set up the press and said, ‘We are eleven people; it is fitting to get one more. Hire one for wages.’ The sugarcane owner said, ‘I myself will be the helper,’ and after having the shed filled with sugarcane, he became their helper. They each performed their respective tasks. After the sugarcane juice was cooked by the syrup-cook and the molasses was bound by the molasses-binder, and after the shares were weighed and given out by the sugarcane owner, they took their respective shares, handed the sugarcane shed back to the owner, and, in the same way, worked in the other four sheds and then departed.

Tattha pañca yantasālā viya pañca pasādā daṭṭhabbā. Pañca ucchuvāṭā viya pañca ārammaṇāni. Ekādasa vicaraṇakayantavāhā viya ekādasa vipākacittāni. Pañca ucchusālāsāmino viya pañcaviññāṇāni. Paṭhamakasālāyaṃ sāmikena saddhiṃ dvādasannaṃ janānaṃ ekatova hutvā katakammānaṃ bhāgaggahaṇakālo viya ekādasannaṃ vipākacittānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇena saddhiṃ ekato hutvā cakkhudvāre rūpārammaṇe sakasakakiccakaraṇakālo. Sālāsāmikassa sālāya sampaṭicchanakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇassa dvārasaṅkantiakaraṇaṃ. Dutiya tatiya catuttha pañcamasālāya dvādasannaṃ ekato hutvā katakammānaṃ bhāgaggahaṇakālo viya ekādasannaṃ vipākacittānaṃ kāyaviññāṇena saddhiṃ ekato hutvā kāyadvāre phoṭṭhabbārammaṇe sakasakakiccakaraṇakālo. Sālāsāmikassa sālāya sampaṭicchanakālo viya kāyaviññāṇassa dvārasaṅkantiakaraṇaṃ veditabbaṃ. Ettāvatā tihetukakammena paṭisandhi tihetukā hotīti vāro kathito. Yā pana tena duhetukapaṭisandhi hoti, sā paṭicchannāva hutvā gatā.

Therein, the five sensitive faculties should be seen as like the five press sheds. The five objects are like the five sugarcane fields. The eleven resultant consciousnesses are like the eleven wandering press operators. The five sense-consciousnesses are like the five owners of the sugarcane sheds. Just as the time when the twelve people, together with the owner, having come together in the first shed, take their shares for the work they have done, so too is the time when the eleven resultant consciousnesses, together with eye-consciousness, having come together, perform their respective functions regarding a visible object at the eye-door. Just as the time when the owner of the shed takes back the shed, so too is the eye-consciousness not making a transition to another door. In the second, third, fourth, and fifth sheds... just as the time when the twelve people, having come together, take their shares for the work they have done, so too is the time when the eleven resultant consciousnesses, together with body-consciousness, having come together, perform their respective functions regarding a tangible object at the body-door. Just as the time when the owner of the shed takes back the shed, so too should the body-consciousness not making a transition to another door be understood. Thus far, the section stating, ‘Due to three-rooted kamma, rebirth-linking is three-rooted,’ has been explained. As for that two-rooted rebirth-linking which arises from it, it has passed by as if concealed.

Idāni duhetukakammena duhetukā paṭisandhi hotīti vāro kathetabbo. Duhetukena hi somanassasahagataasaṅkhārikacittena kamme āyūhite taṃsadiseneva duhetukavipākacittena gahitapaṭisandhikassa vuttanayeneva cakkhudvāre [P 0.0276] ‘iṭṭhārammaṇe’ āpāthamāgate tayo moghavārā. Duhetukasomanassasahagataasaṅkhārikajavanāvasāne taṃsadisameva mūlabhavaṅgasaṅkhātaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ. Sasaṅkhārikajavanāvasāne taṃsadisameva āgantukabhavaṅgasaṅkhātaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ. ‘Iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe’ dvinnaṃ upekkhāsahagatajavanānaṃ avasāne tādisāneva dve tadārammaṇāni uppajjanti. Idha ekekasmiṃ [V 0.0313] dvāre aṭṭha aṭṭha katvā samacattālīsa cittāni. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana cakkhudvāre aṭṭha, sotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇāni cattārīti dvādasa honti. Evaṃ ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite dvādasa [M 0.0316] vipākacittāni uppajjanti. Ambopamapañcaniyāmakathā pākatikā eva. Duhetukasesacittattayasadisavipākena gahitapaṭisandhikepi eseva nayo. Yantavāhopamāya panettha satta yantavāhā. Tehi tattha yante nāma sajjite sālāsāmikaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ katvā vuttanayānusārena yojanā veditabbā. Ettāvatā duhetukakammena duhetukapaṭisandhi hotīti vāro kathito.

Now, the section stating, ‘Due to two-rooted kamma, two-rooted rebirth-linking occurs,’ should be explained. For when kamma is generated by an unprompted, two-rooted consciousness accompanied by joy, for one whose rebirth-linking is taken by a similar two-rooted resultant consciousness, in the eye-door, when a desirable object comes into range, there are three futile occasions, according to the method stated. At the end of the unprompted, two-rooted impulsions accompanied by joy, the registering consciousness, designated as the root life-continuum and of the same kind, arises. At the end of the prompted impulsions, the registering consciousness, designated as the adventitious life-continuum and of the same kind, arises. When a neutral desirable object comes into range, at the end of the two impulsions accompanied by equanimity, two registering consciousnesses of the same kind arise. Here, at each door, there being eight each, there are forty consciousnesses in total. However, by taking what has not yet been taken, there are eight at the eye-door, and the four which are ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness, making twelve. Thus, when kamma is generated by a single volition, twelve resultant consciousnesses arise. The Mango Simile and the discourse on the Fivefold Order are as they are by nature. For one whose rebirth-linking is taken by a resultant consciousness similar to the remaining three types of two-rooted consciousness, this is the same method. Here, in the simile of the press operators, there are seven press operators. When the press is set up by them there, the application should be understood according to the method stated, making the shed owner the eighth. Thus far, the section stating, ‘Due to two-rooted kamma, two-rooted rebirth-linking occurs,’ has been explained.

Idāni ahetukapaṭisandhikathā hoti – catunnañhi duhetukakusalacittānaṃ aññatarena kamme āyūhite kusalavipākaupekkhāsahagatāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātucittena gahitapaṭisandhikassa paṭisandhi kammasadisāti na vattabbā. Kammañhi duhetukaṃ paṭisandhi ahetukā. Tassa vuḍḍhippattassa cakkhudvāre ‘iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe’ āpāthamāgate purimanayeneva tayo moghavārā veditabbā. Catunnaṃ pana duhetukakusalacittānaṃ aññatarajavanassa pariyosāne ahetukacittaṃ tadārammaṇabhāvena patiṭṭhāti. Taṃ ‘mūlabhavaṅgaṃ’‘tadārammaṇa’nti dve nāmāni labhati. Evamettha cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ upekkhāsahagatasantīraṇaṃ tadārammaṇampi upekkhāsahagatamevāti tesu ekaṃ gahetvā gaṇanūpagāni tīṇeva honti.

Now, the discussion on rootless rebirth-linking occurs. For, when kamma has been accumulated by one of the four wholesome consciousnesses with two root-causes, it should not be said that the rebirth-linking of a person whose rebirth-linking has been taken by a wholesome-resultant, rootless mind-consciousness-element consciousness accompanied by equanimity is similar to the kamma. For the kamma has two root-causes, while the rebirth-linking is rootless. When that person has reached growth and a desirable-neutral object comes into focus at the eye-door, three futile occasions should be understood in the same way as before. Furthermore, at the end of the javana of one of the four wholesome consciousnesses with two root-causes, a rootless consciousness is established as a registering consciousness. That consciousness obtains two names: 'root-bhavaṅga' and 'registering consciousness'. Thus, here, the eye-consciousness, the receiving consciousness, the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity, and the registering consciousness are also accompanied by equanimity. Therefore, taking one of them—the investigating and registering consciousnesses—the consciousnesses that are counted are only three.

‘Iṭṭhārammaṇe’ pana santīraṇampi tadārammaṇampi somanassasahagatameva. Tesu ekaṃ gahetvā purimāni tīṇi cattāri honti. Evaṃ pañcasu dvāresu cattāri cattāri katvā ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite vīsati vipākacittāni uppajjantīti [P 0.0277] veditabbāni. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana cakkhudvāre cattāri sotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇāni cattārīti aṭṭha honti. Idaṃ ‘ahetukaṭṭhakaṃ’ nāma. Idaṃ manussalokena gahitaṃ.

Furthermore, in the case of a desirable object, both the investigating consciousness and the registering consciousness are accompanied by joy. Taking one of them, the previous three become four. Thus, it should be known that when kamma has been accumulated by a single volition, making four in each of the five doors, twenty resultant consciousnesses arise. However, by taking what has not yet been taken, there are four at the eye-door and the four which are ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness; thus there are eight. This is called the 'rootless octad.' This is taken with reference to the human world.

Catūsu pana apāyesu pavatte labbhati. Yadā hi mahāmoggallānatthero niraye padumaṃ māpetvā padumakaṇṇikāya nisinno nerayikānaṃ dhammakathaṃ kathesi, tadā tesaṃ theraṃ passantānaṃ kusalavipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppajjati. Saddaṃ suṇantānaṃ sotaviññāṇaṃ, candanavane divāvihāraṃ nisīditvā gatassa cīvaragandhaghāyanakāle ghānaviññāṇaṃ, nirayaggiṃ nibbāpetuṃ devaṃ vassāpetvā pānīyadānakāle jivhāviññāṇaṃ, mandamandavātasamuṭṭhāpanakāle kāyaviññāṇanti evaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīni pañca[M 0.0317], ekaṃ sampaṭicchanaṃ, dve santīraṇānīti ahetukaṭṭhakaṃ labbhati[V 0.0314]. Nāgasupaṇṇavemānikapetānampi akusalena paṭisandhi hoti. Pavatte kusalaṃ vipaccati. Tathā cakkavattino maṅgalahatthiassādīnaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva ‘iṭṭhaiṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇesu’ kusalajavanavasena kathāmaggo.

Furthermore, in the four woeful states, it is obtained during the course of existence. For when the Elder Mahāmoggallāna created a lotus in hell and, seated upon its pericarp, delivered a Dhamma talk to the hell-beings, at that time, for those seeing the Elder, wholesome-resultant eye-consciousness arises. For those hearing the sound, wholesome-resultant ear-consciousness arises. At the time of smelling the fragrance of the robe of one who had gone there after sitting for the day-sojourn in the sandalwood forest, wholesome-resultant nose-consciousness arises. At the time of being given drinking water after a deva was made to send rain to extinguish the hell-fire, wholesome-resultant tongue-consciousness arises. At the time of a gentle breeze being caused to arise, wholesome-resultant body-consciousness arises. Thus, the five consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness, one receiving consciousness, and two investigating consciousnesses—in this way the rootless octad is obtained. For nāgas, supaṇṇas, and vemānika petas also, rebirth-linking occurs through the unwholesome. In the course of existence, the wholesome ripens. Similarly for the auspicious elephant, horse, and so on, of a wheel-turning monarch. This, firstly, is the course of discussion by way of wholesome javana in relation to desirable and desirable-neutral objects.

‘Iṭṭhārammaṇe’ pana catūsu somanassasahagatākusalacittesu javitesu kusalavipākaṃ somanassasahagatāhetukacittaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hoti. ‘Iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe’ catūsu upekkhāsahagatalobhasampayuttesu javitesu kusalavipākaṃ upekkhāsahagatāhetukacittaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hoti. Yaṃ pana ‘javanena tadārammaṇaṃ niyametabba’nti vuttaṃ taṃ kusalaṃ sandhāya vuttanti veditabbaṃ. Domanassasahagatajavanānantaraṃ tadārammaṇaṃ uppajjamānaṃ kiṃ uppajjatīti? Akusalavipākāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātucittaṃ uppajjati.

Furthermore, in the case of a desirable object, when the four unwholesome consciousnesses accompanied by joy have run as javana, the wholesome-resultant, rootless consciousness accompanied by joy becomes the registering consciousness. In the case of a desirable-neutral object, when the four consciousnesses associated with greed and accompanied by equanimity have run as javana, the wholesome-resultant, rootless consciousness accompanied by equanimity becomes the registering consciousness. However, it should be known that what was said, 'the registering consciousness should be determined by the javana,' was said with reference to wholesome javana. Immediately after a javana accompanied by displeasure, when a registering consciousness arises, what arises? The unwholesome-resultant, rootless mind-consciousness-element consciousness arises.

Idaṃ pana javanaṃ kusalatthāya vā akusalatthāya vā ko niyāmetīti? Āvajjanañceva voṭṭhabbanañca. Āvajjanena hi yoniso āvaṭṭite voṭṭhabbanena yoniso vavatthāpite javanaṃ akusalaṃ bhavissatīti aṭṭhānametaṃ. Āvajjanena [P 0.0278] ayoniso āvaṭṭite voṭṭhabbanena ayoniso vavatthāpite javanaṃ kusalaṃ bhavissatītipi aṭṭhānametaṃ. Ubhayena pana yoniso āvaṭṭite vavatthāpite ca javanaṃ kusalaṃ hoti, ayoniso akusalanti veditabbaṃ.

Furthermore, what determines this javana to be for the purpose of the wholesome or the unwholesome? Both adverting and determining. For, when the bhavaṅga has been turned by adverting through wise attention, and it has been defined by determining through wise attention, that the javana will be unwholesome—this is not a possible case. And when the bhavaṅga has been turned by adverting through unwise attention, and it has been defined by determining through unwise attention, that the javana will be wholesome—this too is not a possible case. However, it should be known that when by both it has been turned and defined through wise attention, the javana is wholesome; and through unwise attention, it is unwholesome.

‘Iṭṭhārammaṇe’ pana kaṅkhato uddhatassa ca tadārammaṇaṃ kiṃ hotīti? Iṭṭhārammaṇasmiṃ kaṅkhatu vā mā vā, uddhato vā hotu mā vā, kusalavipākāhetukasomanassacittameva tadārammaṇaṃ hoti, ‘iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe’ ‘kusalavipākāhetukaupekkhāsahagata’nti, ayaṃ panettha saṅkhepato atthadīpano mahādhammarakkhitattheravādo nāma. Somanassasahagatasmiñhi javane javite pañca tadārammaṇāni gavesitabbānīti. Upekkhāsahagatasmiṃ javane javite cha gavesitabbānīti.

Furthermore, in the case of a desirable object, for one who is doubtful and for one who is restless, what is the registering consciousness? Regarding a desirable object, whether one is doubtful or not, whether one is restless or not, only the wholesome-resultant, rootless consciousness accompanied by joy is the registering consciousness. In the case of a desirable-neutral object, it is the wholesome-resultant, rootless consciousness accompanied by equanimity. This here is the brief explanation of the meaning, called the doctrine of the Elder Mahādhammarakkhita. For when a javana accompanied by joy has run, five registering consciousnesses are to be sought. When a javana accompanied by equanimity has run, six are to be sought.

Atha yadā somanassasahagatapaṭisandhikassa pavatte jhānaṃ nibbattetvā pamādena parihīnajjhānassa ‘paṇītadhammo me naṭṭho’ti paccavekkhato vippaṭisāravasena [M 0.0318] domanassaṃ uppajjati, tadā kiṃ uppajjati? ‘Somanassānantarañhi domanassaṃ domanassānantarañca somanassaṃ’ paṭṭhāne paṭisiddhaṃ. Mahaggatadhammaṃ ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇampi tattheva paṭisiddhanti? Kusalavipākā vā akusalavipākā vā upekkhāsahagatāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātu uppajjati[V 0.0315], kimassā āvajjananti? ‘Bhavaṅgāvajjanānaṃ viya natthassā āvajjanakicca’nti. ‘Etāni tāva attano ninnattā ca ciṇṇattā ca samudācārattā ca uppajjantu, ayaṃ kathaṃ uppajjatī’ti? ‘Yathā nirodhassa anantarapaccayaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ, nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa phalasamāpatticittaṃ, ariyamaggacittaṃ, maggānantarāni phalacittāni, evaṃ asantepi āvajjane, ninnaciṇṇasamudācārabhāvena uppajjati. Vinā hi āvajjanena cittaṃ uppajjati, ārammaṇena pana vinā nuppajjatī’ti. ‘Atha kimassārammaṇa’nti? ‘Rūpādīsu parittadhammesu aññataraṃ. Etesu hi yadeva tasmiṃ samaye āpāthamāgataṃ hoti, taṃ ārabbha etaṃ cittaṃ uppajjatī’ti veditabbaṃ.

Then, when grief arises by way of regret for a person—one whose rebirth-linking was accompanied by joy, who, in the course of existence, developed jhāna but later lost it through negligence and now reflects, “My excellent state is lost!”—what arises then? For in the Paṭṭhāna it is prohibited for grief to arise immediately after joy, and for joy to arise immediately after grief. And when javana has run its course taking a sublime state as its object, is registering consciousness also prohibited there? A rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity, which is either wholesome-resultant or unwholesome-resultant, arises. What is its adverting? It has no function of adverting, like bhavaṅga and adverting. Let those arise due to their own inclination, repeated practice, and frequent occurrence; how does this one arise? Just as the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is the proximity condition for the attainment of cessation, and for one emerging from cessation, the fruition-attainment consciousness, the noble path consciousness, and the fruition consciousnesses immediately following the path arise—so too, this arises even without adverting and without the state of inclination, repeated practice, and frequent occurrence. For consciousness can arise without adverting, but it cannot arise without an object. Then what is its object? Any one among the limited states, such as form. For it should be understood that this consciousness arises taking as its object whatever among these has come into range at that time.

Idāni sabbesampi [P 0.0279] etesaṃ cittānaṃ pākaṭabhāvatthaṃ ayaṃ pakiṇṇakanayo vutto –

Now, for the purpose of clarifying all these consciousnesses, this miscellaneous method is stated:

Suttaṃ dovāriko ca, gāmillo ambo koliyakena ca;

Jaccandho pīṭhasappī ca, visayaggāho ca upanissayamatthasoti.

The thread and the doorkeeper, the villager, the mango with the sugarcane-presser; the one blind from birth and the stool-crawler, and the grasping of an object—for the sake of the meaning of decisive support.

Tattha ‘sutta’nti, eko panthamakkaṭako pañcasu disāsu suttaṃ pasāretvā jālaṃ katvā majjhe nipajjati. Paṭhamadisāya pasāritasutte pāṇakena vā paṭaṅgena vā makkhikāya vā pahaṭe nipannaṭṭhānato calitvā nikkhamitvā suttānusārena gantvā tassa yūsaṃ pivitvā punaāgantvā tattheva nipajjati. Dutiyadisādīsu pahaṭakālepi evameva karoti.

Here, regarding ‘the thread’: a certain path-spider spreads a thread in five directions, makes a web, and lies in the middle. When a small creature, a grasshopper, or a fly strikes the thread spread in the first direction, it moves from its resting place, goes out following the thread, drinks its fluid, and then returns to lie there again. It does the same when something strikes the threads in the other directions.

Tattha pañcasu disāsu pasāritasuttaṃ viya pañcapasādā. Majjhe nipannamakkaṭako viya cittaṃ. Pāṇakādīhi suttaghaṭṭanakālo viya ārammaṇena pasādassa ghaṭṭitakālo. Majjhe nipannamakkaṭakassa calanaṃ viya pasādaghaṭṭanakaṃ ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭitakālo. Suttānusārena gamanakālo viya vīthicittappavatti. Sīse vijjhitvā [M 0.0319] yūsapivanaṃ viya javanassa ārammaṇe javitakālo. Punaāgantvā majjhe nipajjanaṃ viya cittassa hadayavatthumeva nissāya pavattanaṃ.

Therein, the five sensitivities are like the thread spread out in five directions. Consciousness is like the spider lying in the middle. The moment the thread is struck by creatures is like the moment the sensitivity is struck by an object. The stirring of the spider lying in the middle is like the moment the life-continuum is adverted by the functional mind-element taking the object that strikes the sensitivity. The movement along the thread is like the process of the cognitive series. Piercing the head and drinking the fluid is like the moment of the javana's running on the object. Returning and lying back down in the middle is like the consciousness's occurrence depending solely on the heart-base.

Idaṃ opammaṃ kiṃ dīpeti? Ārammaṇena pasāde ghaṭṭite pasādavatthukacittato hadayarūpavatthukacittaṃ paṭhamataraṃ uppajjatīti dīpeti. Ekekaṃ ārammaṇaṃ dvīsu dvīsu dvāresu āpāthamāgacchatītipi.

What does this simile illustrate? It illustrates that when a sensitivity is struck by an object, the consciousness based on the heart-base arises earlier than the consciousness based on the sensitivity. It also illustrates that each single object comes into the range of two doors at a time.

‘Dovāriko’ti[V 0.0316], eko rājā sayanagato niddāyati. Tassa paricārako pāde parimajjanto nisīdi. Badhiradovāriko dvāre ṭhito. Tayo paṭihārā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhitā. Atheko paccantavāsī manusso paṇṇākāraṃ ādāya āgantvā dvāraṃ ākoṭesi. Badhiradovāriko saddaṃ na suṇāti. Pādaparimajjako saññaṃ adāsi. Tāya saññāya dvāraṃ vivaritvā passi. Paṭhamapaṭihāro paṇṇākāraṃ gahetvā dutiyassa adāsi, dutiyo tatiyassa, tatiyo rañño. Rājā paribhuñji.

Regarding ‘the doorkeeper’: a certain king lay asleep in his bed. His attendant sat massaging his feet. A deaf doorkeeper stood at the door. Three gatekeepers stood in succession. Then a certain border-dweller came bringing a tribute and knocked at the door. The deaf doorkeeper did not hear the sound. The foot-massager gave a sign. By that sign, the doorkeeper opened the door and saw. The first gatekeeper took the tribute and gave it to the second, the second to the third, and the third to the king. The king consumed it.

Tattha [P 0.0280] so rājā viya javanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pādaparimajjako viya āvajjanaṃ. Badhiradovāriko viya cakkhuviññāṇaṃ. Tayo paṭihārā viya sampaṭicchanādīni tīṇi vīthicittāni. Paccantavāsino paṇṇākāraṃ ādāya āgantvā dvārākoṭanaṃ viya ārammaṇassa pasādaghaṭṭanaṃ. Pādaparimajjakena saññāya dinnakālo viya kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭitakālo. Tena dinnasaññāya badhiradovārikassa dvāravivaraṇakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇassa ārammaṇe dassanakiccasādhanakālo. Paṭhamapaṭihārena paṇṇākārassa gahitakālo viya vipākamanodhātuyā ārammaṇassa sampaṭicchitakālo. Paṭhamena dutiyassa dinnakālo viya vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa santīraṇakālo. Dutiyena tatiyassa dinnakālo viya kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa vavatthāpitakālo. Tatiyena rañño dinnakālo viya voṭṭhabbanena javanassa niyyāditakālo. Rañño paribhogakālo viya javanassa ārammaṇarasānubhavanakālo.

Herein, the javana should be seen as that king. Adverting is like the foot-massager. Eye-consciousness is like the deaf doorkeeper. The three process-consciousnesses beginning with receiving are like the three gatekeepers. The striking of the sensitivity by the object is like the border-dweller coming with a tribute and knocking at the door. The moment the life-continuum was adverted by the functional mind-element is like the moment the foot-massager gave the sign. The moment eye-consciousness accomplished the function of seeing the object is like the moment the deaf doorkeeper opened the door by the sign given by him. The moment the object was received by the resultant mind-element is like the moment the tribute was taken by the first gatekeeper. The moment the object was investigated by the resultant mind-consciousness-element is like the moment it was given to the second by the first. The moment the object was determined by the functional mind-consciousness-element is like the moment it was given to the third by the second. The moment the object was delivered to the javana by the determining consciousness is like the moment it was given to the king by the third. The moment of the javana’s experiencing the taste of the object is like the moment of the king’s enjoyment.

Idaṃ opammaṃ kiṃ dīpeti? Ārammaṇassa pasādaghaṭṭamattanameva kiccaṃ, kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgāvaṭṭanamattameva, cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ dassanasampaṭicchanasantīraṇavavatthāpanamattāneva kiccāni. Ekantena pana javanameva ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhotīti dīpeti.

What does this simile illustrate? It illustrates that the object's function is merely to strike the sensitivity; the functional mind-element's function is merely to advert the life-continuum; and the functions of eye-consciousness and so forth are merely seeing, receiving, investigating, and determining. But it illustrates that, exclusively, it is only the javana that experiences the taste of the object.

‘Gāmillo’ti[M 0.0320], sambahulā gāmadārakā antaravīthiyaṃ paṃsukīḷaṃ kīḷanti. Tatthekassa hatthe kahāpaṇo paṭihaññi. So ‘mayhaṃ hatthe paṭihataṃ, kiṃ nu kho eta’nti āha. Atheko ‘paṇḍaraṃ eta’nti āha. Aparo saha paṃsunā gāḷhaṃ gaṇhi. Añño ‘puthulaṃ caturassaṃ eta’nti āha. Aparo ‘kahāpaṇo eso’ti āha. Atha naṃ āharitvā mātu adāsi. Sā kamme upanesi.

Regarding the word ‘Gāmillo’: Many village boys were playing a dust game in the street. There, a coin struck the hand of one of them. He said, “This thing that has struck my hand, what could it be?” Then one said, “It is white.” Another grasped it tightly along with the dust. Another said, “It is broad and square.” Another said, “This is a coin.” Then, having brought it, he gave it to his mother. She put it to use in commerce.

Tattha [V 0.0317] sambahulānaṃ dārakānaṃ antaravīthiyaṃ kīḷantānaṃ nisinnakālo viya bhavaṅgacittappavatti daṭṭhabbā. Kahāpaṇassa hatthe paṭihatakālo viya ārammaṇena pasādassa ghaṭṭitakālo. ‘Kiṃ nu kho eta’nti vuttakālo viya taṃ ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅgassa āvaṭṭitakālo. ‘Paṇḍaraṃ eta’nti vuttakālo viya cakkhuviññāṇena dassanakiccassa sādhitakālo. Saha paṃsunā gāḷhaṃ gahitakālo viya vipākamanodhātuyā [P 0.0281] ārammaṇassa sampaṭicchitakālo. ‘Puthulaṃ caturassaṃ eta’nti vuttakālo viya vipākamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa santīraṇakālo. ‘Eso kahāpaṇo’ti vuttakālo viya kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātuyā ārammaṇassa vavatthāpitakālo. Mātarā kamme upanītakālo viya javanassa ārammaṇarasānubhavanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Herein, the time when many boys were sitting and playing in the street is to be seen as the occurrence of the life-continuum consciousness. The time the coin struck the hand is like the time the sense faculty was struck by the object. The time “What could this be?” was said is like the time the life-continuum was adverted by the functional mind-element, having taken that object. The time “It is white” was said is like the time the function of seeing was accomplished by eye-consciousness. The time it was tightly grasped along with the dust is like the time the object was received by the resultant mind-element. The time “It is broad and square” was said is like the time the object was investigated by the resultant mind-consciousness-element. The time “This is a coin” was said is like the time the object was determined by the functional mind-consciousness-element. The time it was put to use in commerce by the mother is to be understood as the javana’s experiencing the taste of the object.

Idaṃ opammaṃ kiṃ dīpeti? Kiriyamanodhātu adisvāva bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti, vipākamanodhātu adisvāva sampaṭicchati, vipākamanoviññāṇadhātu adisvāva santīreti, kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātu adisvāva vavatthāpeti, javanaṃ adisvāva ārammaṇarasaṃ anubhoti. Ekantena pana cakkhuviññāṇameva dassanakiccaṃ sādhetīti dīpeti.

What does this simile illustrate? It illustrates that the functional mind-element adverts the life-continuum without seeing; the resultant mind-element receives without seeing; the resultant mind-consciousness-element investigates without seeing; the functional mind-consciousness-element determines without seeing; and the javana experiences the taste of the object without seeing. It illustrates that exclusively, only eye-consciousness accomplishes the function of seeing.

‘Ambo koliyakena cā’ti, idaṃ heṭṭhā vuttaṃ ambopamañca ucchusālāsāmikopamañca sandhāya vuttaṃ.

“And the Koliyan’s mango”—this was said with reference to the mango simile and the simile of the sugarcane-mill owner mentioned previously.

‘Jaccandho pīṭhasappī cā’ti, ubhopi kira te nagaradvāre sālāyaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tattha pīṭhasappī āha – ‘bho andhaka, kasmā tvaṃ idha sussamāno vicarasi, asuko padeso subhikkho bahvannapāno, kiṃ tattha gantvā sukhena jīvituṃ na vaṭṭatī’ti? ‘Mayhaṃ tāva tayā ācikkhitaṃ, tuyhaṃ pana tattha gantvā sukhena jīvituṃ kiṃ na vaṭṭatī’ti? ‘Mayhaṃ gantuṃ pādā natthī’ti. ‘Mayhampi passituṃ cakkhūni natthī’ti. ‘Yadi evaṃ, tava pādā hontu, mama cakkhūnī’ti ubhopi ‘sādhū’ti [M 0.0321] sampaṭicchitvā jaccandho pīṭhasappiṃ khandhaṃ āropesi. So tassa khandhe nisīditvā vāmahatthenassa sīsaṃ parikkhipitvā dakkhiṇahatthena ‘imasmiṃ ṭhāne mūlaṃ āvaritvā ṭhitaṃ, imasmiṃ pāsāṇo, vāmaṃ muñca dakkhiṇaṃ gaṇha, dakkhiṇaṃ muñca vāmaṃ gaṇhā’ti maggaṃ niyametvā ācikkhati. Evaṃ jaccandhassa pādā pīṭhasappissa cakkhūnīti ubhopi sampayogena icchitaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā sukhena jīviṃsu.

“And a man blind from birth and a cripple”—it is said that both of them were sitting in a hall at the city gate. There, the cripple said, “Hey blind man, why do you wander around here withering away? Such-and-such a place is prosperous with much food and drink. Why is it not proper to go there and live happily?” The blind man replied, “You have indeed told me, but why is it not proper for you to go there and live happily?” The cripple said, “I have no legs to go.” The blind man said, “And I have no eyes to see.” “If that is so, let it be your legs and my eyes.” Both agreed, saying, “Good.” The man blind from birth made the cripple ascend onto his shoulder. Sitting on his shoulder, he embraced the blind man’s head with his left hand and with his right hand directed him, saying, “In this place, a root stands blocking the way; in this place, a rock; release the left, take the right; release the right, take the left,” thus determining the path and telling him. Thus, with the blind man’s legs and the cripple’s eyes, both, by their cooperation, went to the desired place and lived happily.

Tattha [V 0.0318] jaccandho viya rūpakāyo, pīṭhasappī viya arūpakāyo. Pīṭhasappinā vinā jaccandhassa disaṃ gantuṃ gamanābhisaṅkhārassa anibbattitakālo [P 0.0282] viya rūpassa arūpena vinā ādānagahaṇacopanaṃ pāpetuṃ asamatthatā. Jaccandhena vinā pīṭhasappissa disaṃ gantuṃ gamanābhisaṅkhārassa appavattanaṃ viya pañcavokāre rūpaṃ, vinā arūpassa appavatti. Dvinnampi sampayogena icchitaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā sukhena jīvitakālo viya rūpārūpadhammānaṃ aññamaññayogena sabbakiccesu pavattisambhāvoti. Ayaṃ pañho pañcavokārabhavavasena kathito.

Herein, the material body is to be seen as like the man blind from birth, and the immaterial body as like the cripple. Just as the volition for going of the man blind from birth does not arise to go in any direction without the cripple, so the inability of the material, without the immaterial, to achieve taking, grasping, and moving is to be seen. Just as the volition for going of the cripple does not occur to go in any direction without the man blind from birth, so in the five-constituent existence, without the material, the immaterial does not occur. Just as the time they lived happily having gone to the desired place through the cooperation of both, so too, through the mutual connection of material and immaterial phenomena, the actual state of their occurrence in all functions is to be seen. This question is explained in terms of the five-constituent existence.

‘Visayaggāho’ cāti, cakkhu rūpavisayaṃ gaṇhāti. Sotādīni saddādivisaye.

“And ‘the grasping of objects’” means: the eye grasps the visible-object; the ear and so forth grasp the sound-object and so forth.

‘Upanissayamatthaso’ti, ‘upanissayato’ ca ‘atthato’ ca. Tattha asambhinnattā cakkhussa, āpāthagatattā rūpānaṃ, ālokasannissitaṃ, manasikārahetukaṃ catūhi paccayehi uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ, saddhiṃ sampayuttadhammehi. Tattha matassāpi cakkhu sambhinnaṃ hoti. Jīvato niruddhampi, pittena vā semhena vā ruhirena vā palibuddhampi, cakkhuviññāṇassa paccayo bhavituṃ asakkontaṃ ‘sambhinnaṃ’ nāma hoti. Sakkontaṃ asambhinnaṃ nāma. Sotādīsupi eseva nayo. Cakkhusmiṃ pana asambhinnepi bahiddhā rūpārammaṇe āpāthaṃ anāgacchante cakkhuviññāṇaṃ nuppajjati. Tasmiṃ pana āpāthaṃ āgacchantepi ālokasannissaye asati nuppajjati. Tasmiṃ santepi kiriyamanodhātuyā bhavaṅge anāvaṭṭite nuppajjati. Āvaṭṭiteyeva uppajjati. Evaṃ uppajjamānaṃ sampayuttadhammehi saddhiṃyeva uppajjati. Iti ime cattāro paccaye labhitvā uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇaṃ (ma. ni. 1.306 thokaṃ visadisaṃ).

“By way of strong dependence and meaning” means “by way of strong dependence” and “by way of meaning.” Herein, eye-consciousness arises by four conditions, along with its associated phenomena: due to the intactness of the eye, due to visible forms having come into the field of vision, being dependent on light, and having attention as its cause. In this regard, even the eye of a dead person is destroyed. Even if it has ceased while one is alive, or is obstructed by bile, phlegm, or blood, that which is incapable of being a condition for eye-consciousness is called ‘destroyed.’ That which is capable is called ‘intact.’ The same principle applies to the ear and so forth. But even when the eye is intact, if external visible objects do not come into the field of vision, eye-consciousness does not arise. But even when they do come into the field of vision, if there is no reliance on light, it does not arise. Even when that light is present, if the life-continuum is not adverted by the functional mind-element, it does not arise. It arises only when it is adverted. Thus arising, it arises only together with its associated phenomena. Thus, eye-consciousness arises having obtained these four conditions.

Asambhinnattā [M 0.0322] sotassa, āpāthagatattā saddānaṃ, ākāsasannissitaṃ, manasikārahetukaṃ catūhi paccayehi uppajjati sotaviññāṇaṃ, saddhiṃ sampayuttadhammehi. Tattha ‘ākāsasannissita’nti ākāsasannissayaṃ laddhāva uppajjati, na vinā tena. Na hi pihitakaṇṇacchiddassa sotaviññāṇaṃ pavattati. Sesaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Yathā cettha evaṃ ito paresupi. Visesamattaṃ pana vakkhāma.

Due to four conditions—the unimpaired state of the ear sensitivity, sounds having come into range, dependence on space, and attention as a cause—ear-consciousness arises, together with its associated states. Therein, 'dependence on space' means it arises only having obtained the support of space, not without it. For ear-consciousness does not occur in one whose ear-canal is blocked. The remainder should be understood by the previous method. As it is here, so it is in the subsequent cases. However, we shall state only the distinctive features.

Asambhinnattā ghānassa, āpāthagatattā gandhānaṃ, vāyosannissitaṃ, manasikārahetukaṃ catūhi paccayehi [V 0.0319] uppajjati ghānaviññāṇaṃ[P 0.0283], saddhiṃ sampayuttadhammehi. Tattha ‘vāyosannissita’nti ghānabilaṃ vāyumhi pavisanteyeva uppajjati, tasmiṃ asati nuppajjatīti attho.

Due to four conditions—the unimpaired state of the nose sensitivity, odors having come into range, dependence on the air element, and attention as a cause—nose-consciousness arises, together with its associated states. Therein, 'dependence on the air element' means it arises only when air enters the nasal cavity; if that is not present, it does not arise—this is the meaning.

Asambhinnattā jivhāya, āpāthagatattā rasānaṃ, āposannissitaṃ, manasikārahetukaṃ catūhi paccayehi uppajjati jivhāviññāṇaṃ, saddhiṃ sampayuttadhammehi. Tattha ‘āposannissita’nti jivhātemanaṃ āpaṃ laddhāva uppajjati, na vinā tena. Sukkhajivhānañhi sukkhakhādanīye jivhāya ṭhapitepi jivhāviññāṇaṃ nuppajjateva.

Due to four conditions—the unimpaired state of the tongue sensitivity, flavors having come into range, dependence on the water element, and attention as a cause—tongue-consciousness arises, together with its associated states. Therein, 'dependence on the water element' means it arises only having obtained the water element that moistens the tongue, not without it. For in those with a dry tongue, even when dry food is placed on the tongue, tongue-consciousness does not arise at all.

Asambhinnattā kāyassa, āpāthagatattā phoṭṭhabbānaṃ, pathavisannissitaṃ, manasikārahetukaṃ catūhi paccayehi uppajjati kāyaviññāṇaṃ, saddhiṃ sampayuttadhammehi. Tattha ‘pathavisannissita’nti kāyapasādapaccayaṃ pathavisannissayaṃ laddhāva uppajjati, na tena vinā. Kāyadvārasmiñhi bahiddhāmahābhūtārammaṇaṃ ajjhattikaṃ kāyapasādaṃ ghaṭṭetvā pasādapaccayesu mahābhūtesu paṭihaññati.

Due to four conditions—the unimpaired state of the body sensitivity, tangible objects having come into range, dependence on the earth element, and attention as a cause—body-consciousness arises, together with its associated states. Therein, 'dependence on the earth element' means it arises only having obtained the support of the earth element, which is a condition for the body sensitivity, and not without it. For at the body-door, an external great element as object, having struck the internal body sensitivity, impinges on the great elements that are the supporting conditions for the sensitivity.

Asambhinnattā manassa, āpāthagatattā dhammānaṃ, vatthusannissitaṃ, manasikārahetukaṃ catūhi paccayehi uppajjati manoviññāṇaṃ, saddhiṃ sampayuttadhammehi. Tattha ‘mano’ti bhavaṅgacittaṃ. Taṃ niruddhampi, āvajjanacittassa paccayo bhavituṃ asamatthaṃ mandathāmagatameva pavattamānampi, sambhinnaṃ nāma hoti. Āvajjanassa pana paccayo bhavituṃ samatthaṃ asambhinnaṃ nāma. ‘Āpāthagatattā dhammāna’nti dhammārammaṇe āpāthagate. ‘Vatthusannissita’nti hadayavatthusannissayaṃ laddhāva uppajjati, na tena vinā. Ayampi pañho pañcavokārabhavaṃ [M 0.0323] sandhāya kathito. ‘Manasikārahetuka’nti kiriyamanoviññāṇadhātuyā bhavaṅge āvaṭṭiteyeva uppajjatīti attho. Ayaṃ tāva ‘upanissayamatthaso’ti ettha upanissayavaṇṇanā.

Due to four conditions—the unimpaired state of the mind, mental objects having come into range, dependence on the physical base, and attention as a cause—mind-consciousness arises, together with its associated states. Therein, 'mind' is the bhavaṅga-citta. That bhavaṅga, even when it has ceased, or even while it is occurring, if it has become weak and is incapable of being a condition for the adverting consciousness, is called 'impaired'. On the other hand, that which is capable of being a condition for adverting is called 'unimpaired'. 'Mental objects having come into range' means when a mental object has come into range. 'Dependence on the physical base' means it arises only having obtained the support of the heart-base, not without it. This point is also stated with reference to the five-aggregate existence. 'Attention as a cause' means that it arises only when the functional mind-consciousness-element has adverted towards the bhavaṅga; this is the meaning. This, so far, is the explanation of 'upanissaya' in the phrase 'upanissayamatthaso'.

‘Atthato’ pana cakkhu dassanatthaṃ, sotaṃ savanatthaṃ, ghānaṃ ghāyanatthaṃ, jivhā sāyanatthā, kāyo phusanattho[P 0.0284], mano vijānanattho. Tattha dassanaṃ attho assa. Tañhi tena nipphādetabbanti dassanatthaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Ettāvatā tipiṭakacūḷanāgattheravāde soḷasakamaggo niṭṭhito, saddhiṃ dvādasakamaggena ceva ahetukaṭṭhakena cāti.

As to meaning, however, the eye is for the purpose of seeing, the ear for the purpose of hearing, the nose for the purpose of smelling, the tongue for the purpose of tasting, the body for the purpose of touching, and the mind for the purpose of cognizing. Therein, 'seeing is its purpose' (dassanaṃ attho assa). For that can be accomplished by it; therefore, it is 'for the purpose of seeing' (dassanatthaṃ). This is the same method for the remaining cases as well. With this, in the doctrine of the Elder Tipiṭaka Cūḷanāga, the sixteenfold division is concluded, together with the twelvefold division and the eightfold rootless division.

Idāni moravāpīvāsīmahādattattheravāde dvādasakamaggakathā hoti. Tattha sāketapañhaussadakittanahetukittanāni [V 0.0320] pākatikāneva. Ayaṃ pana thero asaṅkhārikasasaṅkhārikesu dosaṃ disvā ‘asaṅkhārikaṃ asaṅkhārikameva vipākaṃ deti, no sasaṅkhārikaṃ; sasaṅkhārikampi sasaṅkhārikameva no asaṅkhārika’nti āha. Javanena cesa cittaniyāmaṃ na katheti. Ārammaṇena pana vedanāniyāmaṃ katheti. Tenassa vipākuddhāre dvādasakamaggo nāma jāto. Dasakamaggopi, ahetukaṭṭhakampi ettheva paviṭṭhaṃ.

Now, the discourse on the twelvefold division occurs in the doctrine of the Elder Mahādatta, who dwelt at Moravāpī. Therein, the Sāketa question, the Ussada enumeration, and the Hetu enumeration are as in the original. But this elder, seeing a fault in the unprompted and prompted states, said: 'Unprompted kamma gives only an unprompted resultant, not a prompted one; and prompted kamma also gives only a prompted resultant, not an unprompted one.' And he does not state the fixed order of consciousness by way of javana, but he states the fixed order of feeling by way of the object. Therefore, in his exposition of resultants, what is called the twelvefold division arose. The tenfold division and the eightfold rootless division are also included herein.

Tatrāyaṃ nayo – somanassasahagatatihetukaasaṅkhārikacittena hi kamme āyūhite tādiseneva vipākacittena gahitapaṭisandhikassa vuḍḍhippattassa cakkhudvāre ‘iṭṭhārammaṇe’ āpāthagate heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva tayo moghavārā honti. Tassa kusalato cattāri somanassasahagatāni, akusalato cattāri, kiriyato pañcāti imesaṃ terasannaṃ cittānaṃ aññatarena javitapariyosāne tadārammaṇaṃ patiṭṭhahamānaṃ somanassasahagataasaṅkhārikatihetukacittampi duhetukacittampi patiṭṭhāti. Evamassa cakkhudvāre cakkhuviññāṇādīni tīṇi, tadārammaṇāni dveti, pañca gaṇanūpagacittāni honti.

Herein, this is the method: For when kamma has been accumulated by an unprompted, three-rooted consciousness accompanied by joy, in the case of a person who has taken rebirth-linking with a resultant consciousness of that same kind and has reached maturity, when a desirable object has come into range at the eye-door, three futile occasions occur in the way stated previously. For that person, at the end of the javana process of any one of these thirteen consciousnesses—four wholesome accompanied by joy, four unwholesome accompanied by joy, and five functional accompanied by joy—when the registering consciousness is being established, both a three-rooted, unprompted consciousness accompanied by joy and a two-rooted consciousness become established. Thus, for this person, in the eye-door process, there are three resultant consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness and two registering consciousnesses, making five consciousnesses that enter into the count.

Ārammaṇena pana vedanaṃ parivattetvā kusalato catunnaṃ, akusalato catunnaṃ, kiriyato catunnanti, dvādasannaṃ upekkhāsahagatacittānaṃ aññatarena javitāvasāne upekkhāsahagatatihetukaasaṅkhārikavipākampi duhetukaasaṅkhārikavipākampi tadārammaṇaṃ hutvā uppajjati. Evamassa cakkhudvāre upekkhāsahagatasantīraṇaṃ, imāni dve tadārammaṇānīti, tīṇi gaṇanūpagacittāni [M 0.0324] honti. Tāni purimehi pañcahi saddhiṃ [P 0.0285] aṭṭha. Sotadvārādīsupi aṭṭha aṭṭhāti ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite samacattālīsa cittāni uppajjanti. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana cakkhudvāre aṭṭha, sotaviññāṇādīni cattārīti, dvādasa honti. Tattha ‘mūlabhavaṅgatā’‘āgantukabhavaṅgatā’‘ambopamaniyāmakathā’ ca vuttanayeneva veditabbā.

However, by altering the feeling by means of the object, at the end of the impulsion of any one of the twelve consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity—four wholesome, four unwholesome, and four functional—either a three-rooted, unprompted resultant consciousness accompanied by equanimity, or a two-rooted, unprompted resultant consciousness, arises as the registering consciousness. Thus, for this person, in the eye-door, there are the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity and these two registering consciousnesses; thus, three consciousnesses that come into the reckoning arise. These, together with the previous five, make eight. In the ear-door and so on, there are also eight each. Thus, when kamma is accumulated by a single volition, exactly forty resultant consciousnesses arise. However, by way of taking what has not yet been taken, in the eye-door there are eight, and the ear-consciousness and others are four; thus, there are twelve. Therein, 'the state of being the root life-continuum,' 'the state of being the guest life-continuum,' and 'the discourse on the simile of the mango and the fixed order' should be understood in the manner already stated.

Somanassasahagatatihetukasasaṅkhārikakusalacittena kamme āyūhitepi upekkhāsahagatatihetukaasaṅkhārikasasaṅkhārikehi kamme āyūhitepi eseva nayo. Tattha yantopamāpi ettha pākatikā eva. Ettāvatā tihetukakammena tihetukapaṭisandhi hotīti vāro kathito. Tihetukakammena duhetukapaṭisandhi hotīti vāro pana paṭicchanno hutvā gato.

This is the same method also when kamma is accumulated by a wholesome consciousness accompanied by joy, with three roots, and prompted, and also when kamma is accumulated by wholesome consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, with three roots, unprompted or prompted. Therein, the simile of the machine is also, here, just as it naturally is. With this much, the section stating, 'rebirth-linking with three roots occurs by means of kamma with three roots,' has been explained. However, the section stating, 'rebirth-linking with two roots occurs by means of kamma with three roots,' has become concealed and has passed.

Idāni [V 0.0321] duhetukakammena duhetukapaṭisandhikathā hoti. Somanassasahagataduhetukaasaṅkhārikacittena hi kamme āyūhite tādiseneva vipākacittena gahitapaṭisandhikassa vuḍḍhippattassa cakkhudvāre iṭṭhārammaṇe āpāthagate heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva tayo moghavārā honti. Duhetukassa pana javanakiriyā natthi. Tasmā kusalato cattāri somanassasahagatāni, akusalato cattārīti imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ aññatarena javitapariyosāne duhetukameva somanassasahagataasaṅkhārikaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hoti. Evamassa cakkhuviññāṇādīni tīṇi, idañca tadārammaṇanti, cattāri gaṇanūpagacittāni honti. ‘Iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe’ pana kusalato upekkhāsahagatānaṃ catunnaṃ, akusalato catunnanti, aṭṭhannaṃ aññatarena javitapariyosāne duhetukameva upekkhāsahagataṃ asaṅkhārikaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ hoti. Evamassa upekkhāsahagatasantīraṇaṃ, idañca tadārammaṇanti, dve gaṇanūpagacittāni honti. Tāni purimehi catūhi saddhiṃ cha. Sotadvārādīsupi cha chāti ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite samatiṃsa cittāni uppajjanti. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana cakkhudvāre cha, sotaviññāṇādīni cattārīti dasa honti. Ambopamaniyāmakathā pākatikā eva. Yantopamā idha na labbhatīti vuttaṃ.

Now, there is the discourse on rebirth-linking with two roots by means of kamma with two roots. Indeed, when kamma is accumulated by a consciousness with two roots, unprompted, and accompanied by joy, for one who has taken rebirth-linking by a resultant consciousness of that same kind and who has reached maturity, when a desirable object has come into range at the eye-door, three futile sections occur in the manner already stated below. However, for a two-rooted person, there is no functional impulsion. Therefore, at the end of the impulsion of any one of these eight consciousnesses—four wholesome accompanied by joy and four unwholesome—only the two-rooted, unprompted registering consciousness accompanied by joy arises. Thus, for this person, there are the three consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness, and this registering consciousness; thus, four consciousnesses that come into the reckoning arise. However, in the case of a desirable-neutral object, at the end of the impulsion of any one of these eight consciousnesses—four wholesome accompanied by equanimity and four unwholesome—only the two-rooted, unprompted registering consciousness accompanied by equanimity arises. Thus, for this person, there are the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity and this registering consciousness; thus, two consciousnesses that come into the reckoning arise. These, together with the previous four, make six. In the ear-door and so on, there are also six each. Thus, when kamma is accumulated by a single volition, exactly thirty consciousnesses arise. However, by way of taking what has not yet been taken, in the eye-door there are six, and the ear-consciousness and others are four; thus, there are ten. The discourse on the simile of the mango and the fixed order is just as it naturally is. It has been said that the simile of the machine is not obtained here.

Somanassasahagataduhetukasasaṅkhārikakusalacittena [M 0.0325][P 0.0286] kamme āyūhitepi upekkhāsahagataduhetukaasaṅkhārikasasaṅkhārikehi kamme āyūhitepi eseva nayo. Ettāvatā duhetukakammena duhetukapaṭisandhi hotīti vāro kathito.

This is the same method also when kamma is accumulated by a wholesome consciousness accompanied by joy, with two roots, and prompted, and also when kamma is accumulated by wholesome consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity, with two roots, unprompted or prompted. With this much, the section stating, 'rebirth-linking with two roots occurs by means of kamma with two roots,' has been explained.

Ahetukapaṭisandhi hotīti vāro pana evaṃ veditabbo – kusalato catūhi ñāṇavippayuttehi kamme āyūhite, kusalavipākāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyā upekkhāsahagatāya paṭisandhiyā gahitāya, kammasadisā paṭisandhīti na vattabbā. Ito paṭṭhāya heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva kathetvā iṭṭhepi iṭṭhamajjhattepi cittappavatti veditabbā. Imassa hi therassa vāde piṇḍajavanaṃ javati. Sesā idaṃ pana javanaṃ kusalatthāya vā akusalatthāya vā ko niyāmetītiādikathā sabbā heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbāti. Ettāvatā moravāpīvāsīmahādattattheravāde dvādasakamaggo niṭṭhito saddhiṃ dasakamaggena ceva ahetukaṭṭhakena ca.

However, the section stating, 'rootless rebirth-linking occurs,' should be understood thus: when kamma is accumulated by the four wholesome consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge, and when rebirth-linking is taken by the rootless wholesome-resultant mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity, it should not be said, 'the rebirth-linking is similar to the kamma.' Starting from this point, having explained in the manner already stated below, the process of consciousness should be understood in the case of both desirable and desirable-neutral objects. Indeed, in the view of this elder, a collective impulsion impels. The remaining discourse, beginning with 'Who determines whether this impulsion is for the sake of the wholesome or for the sake of the unwholesome?', should all be understood in the manner already stated below. With this much, in the view of the Elder Mahādatta, resident of Moravāpī, the twelvefold course is concluded, together with the tenfold course and the rootless octad.

Idāni mahādhammarakkhitattheravāde dasakamaggakathā hoti. Tattha sāketapañhaussadakittanāni pākatikāneva. Hetukittane pana ayaṃ viseso. Tihetukakammaṃ tihetukavipākampi duhetukavipākampi [V 0.0322] ahetukavipākampi deti. Duhetukakammaṃ tihetukameva na deti, itaraṃ deti. Tihetukakammena paṭisandhi tihetukāva hoti; duhetukāhetukā na hoti. Duhetukakammena duhetukāhetukā hoti, tihetukā na hoti. Asaṅkhārikakammaṃ vipākaṃ asaṅkhārikameva deti, no sasaṅkhārikaṃ. Sasaṅkhārikampi sasaṅkhārikameva deti, no asaṅkhārikaṃ. Ārammaṇena vedanā parivattetabbā. Javanaṃ piṇḍajavanameva javati. Ādito paṭṭhāya cittāni kathetabbāni.

Now, in the view of the Elder Mahādhammarakkhita, there is the discourse on the tenfold course. Therein, the expositions on the Sāketa question and the prominent points are just as they naturally are. However, in the exposition of the roots, this is the distinction. Kamma with three roots gives a resultant with three roots, with two roots, and without roots. Kamma with two roots does not give a resultant with three roots; it gives the others. By means of kamma with three roots, rebirth-linking is only with three roots; it is not with two roots or without roots. By means of kamma with two roots, it is with two roots or without roots; it is not with three roots. Unprompted kamma gives only an unprompted result, not a prompted one. Prompted kamma also gives only a prompted result, not an unprompted one. Feeling is to be altered by means of the object. As for impulsion, only a collective impulsion impels. The consciousnesses should be explained starting from the beginning.

Tatrāyaṃ kathā – eko paṭhamakusalacittena kammaṃ āyūhati, paṭhamavipākacitteneva paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhāti. Ayaṃ kammasadisā paṭisandhi. Tassa vuḍḍhippattassa cakkhudvāre ‘iṭṭhārammaṇe’ āpāthagate vuttanayeneva tayo moghavārā honti. Athassa heṭṭhā vuttānaṃ terasannaṃ somanassasahagatajavanānaṃ [P 0.0287] aññatarena javitapariyosāne paṭhamavipākacittameva tadārammaṇaṃ [M 0.0326] hoti. Taṃ ‘mūlabhavaṅgaṃ’ ‘tadārammaṇa’nti dve nāmāni labhati. Evamassa cakkhuviññāṇādīni tīṇi, idañca tadārammaṇanti, cattāri gaṇanūpagacittāni honti. ‘Iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇe’ heṭṭhā vuttānaṃyeva dvādasannaṃ upekkhāsahagatajavanānaṃ aññatarena javitapariyosāne upekkhāsahagataṃ tihetukaṃ asaṅkhārikacittaṃ tadārammaṇatāya pavattati. Taṃ ‘āgantukabhavaṅgaṃ’‘tadārammaṇa’nti dve nāmāni labhati. Evamassa upekkhāsahagatasantīraṇaṃ idañca tadārammaṇanti dve gaṇanūpagacittāni. Tāni purimehi catūhi saddhiṃ cha honti. Evaṃ ekāya cetanāya kamme āyūhite pañcasu dvāresu samatiṃsa cittāni uppajjanti. Aggahitaggahaṇena pana cakkhudvāre cha, sotaviññāṇādīni cattārīti dasa honti. Ambopamaniyāmakathā pākatikāyeva.

Here is the explanation: A certain person accumulates kamma with the first wholesome consciousness and takes rebirth with the first resultant consciousness itself. This is a rebirth that is similar to the kamma. For that person, having reached maturity, when an agreeable object comes into range at the eye-door, three futile processes occur in the manner already stated. Then, for that person, at the end of the impulsion-process by one or another of the thirteen types of impulsion accompanied by joy mentioned previously, the first resultant consciousness itself becomes the tadārammaṇa. It obtains two names: 'root life-continuum' and 'tadārammaṇa.' Thus, for that person, the three consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness, and this tadārammaṇa, are four consciousnesses that are enumerated. In the case of a moderately agreeable object, at the end of the impulsion-process by one or another of the twelve types of impulsion accompanied by equanimity mentioned previously, an unprompted, three-rooted consciousness accompanied by equanimity arises as the tadārammaṇa. It obtains two names: 'adventitious life-continuum' and 'tadārammaṇa.' Thus, for that person, the investigating consciousness accompanied by equanimity and this tadārammaṇa are two enumerated consciousnesses. Together with the previous four, they become six. In this way, when kamma is accumulated by a single volition, thirty consciousnesses arise in the five sense-doors. However, by way of taking up what has not been taken up before, there are ten: six in the eye-door, and four beginning with ear-consciousness. The discussion of the mango simile and the fixed-course simile is as it is naturally.

Dutiyatatiyacatutthakusalacittehi kamme āyūhitepi ettakāneva vipākacittāni honti. Catūhi upekkhāsahagatacittehi āyūhitepi eseva nayo. Idha pana paṭhamaṃ iṭṭhamajjhattārammaṇaṃ dassetabbaṃ. Pacchā iṭṭhārammaṇena vedanā parivattetabbā. Ambopamaniyāmakathā pākatikā eva. Yantopamā na labbhati. ‘Kusalato pana catunnaṃ ñāṇavippayuttānaṃ aññatarena kamme āyūhite’ti ito paṭṭhāya sabbaṃ vitthāretvā ahetukaṭṭhakaṃ kathetabbaṃ. Ettāvatā mahādhammarakkhitattheravāde dasakamaggo niṭṭhito hoti, saddhiṃ ahetukaṭṭhakenāti.
